newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd rebels in Turkey release three foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Kurd rebels in Turkey release three foreigners.

text.p: Two Polish tourists and one Iranian were released on Friday after being kidnapped three days earlier by Kurdish rebels, a Polish embassy spokesman said.
Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels kidnapped the three on Tuesday after setting up a roadblock and stopping a bus in the eastern province of Bingol, the state-run Anatolian news agency said.
The three were freed in Bingol on Friday afternoon and picked up by Turkish security forces for questioning about their ordeal.

PKK guerrillas have kidnapped several dozen foreigners in the past as part of their campaign for independence or autonomy in the largely Kurdish southeast. More than 20,000 people have died in the 12-year conflict.
In 1994, two Finnish tourists were held for three weeks by PKK rebels who said they were in violation of an order that all travellers to the Kurdish region first obtain a "visa."
